## INSTALL LIBRARIES
```{r setup, message=FALSE, warning=FALSE}
# Install once in the Console if missing (not when knitting):
# install.packages(c("AmesHousing", "kableExtra", "knitr", "dplyr", "ggplot2", "car"))

library(AmesHousing)
library(kableExtra)
library(knitr)
library(dplyr)
library(ggplot2)
library(car)

ames <- make_ames()
```

## 1) DATA PREPARATION
```{r}
# Remove 5 houses: The dataset author (De Cock, 2011, data documentation) recommends
# removing houses > 4000 sq ft: 3 are partial sales that do not reflect market value,
# 2 are unusually large homes. (JUSTIFIED)
ames[ames$Gr_Liv_Area > 4000, c("Gr_Liv_Area", "Sale_Price", "Sale_Condition")]
ames <- subset(ames, Gr_Liv_Area <= 4000)
ames <- droplevels(ames)

# Tiny neighbourhoods: a neighbourhood with 1 sale gets leverage = 1 (NaN residuals/Cook's D).
# Merge neighbourhoods with fewer than 3 sales into "Other" (noted as a limitation).
sort(table(ames$Neighborhood))
small_nbhd <- names(which(table(ames$Neighborhood) < 3))
small_nbhd                                            # e.g., Landmark (1), Green_Hills (2)
levels(ames$Neighborhood)[levels(ames$Neighborhood) %in% small_nbhd] <- "Other"
ames$Neighborhood <- relevel(ames$Neighborhood, ref = "North_Ames")

# Relevel quality so Average (largest group) is the baseline
ames$Overall_Qual <- relevel(ames$Overall_Qual, ref = "Average")

# Natural quality order, used for plots and tables
qual_levels <- c("Very_Poor", "Poor", "Fair", "Below_Average", "Average",
                 "Above_Average", "Good", "Very_Good", "Excellent", "Very_Excellent")

# Add transformed response values to the table
ames$Log_Price <- log(ames$Sale_Price)
ames$Price_0.2 <- ames$Sale_Price^0.2

nrow(ames)
```


## 2) PROBLEMATIC OBSERVATIONS (Before Transformation)
```{r}
model <- lm(Sale_Price ~ Year_Built + Year_Remod_Add + Garage_Cars + Lot_Area + Neighborhood +
        Bldg_Type + Central_Air + Overall_Qual * Gr_Liv_Area, data = ames) # Original Model

n <- nobs(model)
p <- length(coef(model)) - 1

# leverage cutoff
hcut <- 2 * (p + 1) / n

# outlier cutoff
rcut <- 4

# cook's distance cutoff
cookcut <- qf(0.5, p + 1, n - p - 1)

# dffits cutoff
fitcut <- 2 * sqrt((p + 1) / n)

# dfbetas cutoff
betacut <- 2 / sqrt(n)

# leverage statistic
h_ii <- hatvalues(model)

# standardized residuals
r_i <- rstandard(model)

# cook's distance
D_i <- cooks.distance(model)

# dffits
dffits_i <- dffits(model)

# dfbetas (one column per coefficient)
dfbetas_i <- dfbetas(model)

# which observations are leverage points?
leverage <- which(h_ii > hcut)

# which observations are regression outliers?
outliers <- which(r_i > rcut | r_i < -rcut)

# which observations are influential by cook's distance?
infl_cook <- which(D_i > cookcut)

# which observations are influential by dffits?
infl_dffits <- which(abs(dffits_i) > fitcut)

# How many of each?
cat("Num of leverage points:\n")
length(leverage)
cat("Num of outliers:\n")
length(outliers)
cat("Num of influential points by cook's distance:\n")
length(infl_cook)
cat("Num of influential point by dffits:\n")
length(infl_dffits)

# Num of influential points by DFBETAS, for each coefficient (neighbourhood dummies hidden)
cat("Num of influential points by DFBETAS (per coefficient):\n")
dfb_counts <- colSums(abs(dfbetas_i) > betacut)
dfb_counts[!grepl("^Neighborhood", names(dfb_counts))]

# Problematic in more than one way:
# outliers that are also influential by dffits
out_and_dffits <- intersect(outliers, infl_dffits)
cat("Outliers that are also influential by dffits:\n")
out_and_dffits

# outliers that are also leverage points
out_and_lev <- intersect(outliers, leverage)
cat("Outliers that are also leverage points:\n")
out_and_lev

knitr::kable(ames[out_and_dffits, c("Sale_Price", "Gr_Liv_Area", "Overall_Qual", "Neighborhood", "Sale_Condition")],
             caption = "Houses that are both outliers and influential (DFFITS)") %>%
  kable_styling(full_width = FALSE)

# Who are these houses?
knitr::kable(ames[out_and_lev, c("Sale_Price", "Gr_Liv_Area", "Overall_Qual", "Neighborhood", "Sale_Condition")],
             caption = "Houses that are both outliers and leverage points") %>%
  kable_styling(full_width = FALSE)

par(mfrow = c(1, 1))
plot(fitted(model), ames$Sale_Price, pch = 16, cex = 0.5, col = "grey70",
     main = "Response vs Fitted, problematic observations highlighted (original model)",
     xlab = "Fitted Sale_Price", ylab = "Sale_Price")
abline(0, 1, lty = 2, lwd = 2)

points(fitted(model)[leverage],  ames$Sale_Price[leverage],  col = "blue", pch = 1)
points(fitted(model)[infl_cook], ames$Sale_Price[infl_cook], col = "orange", pch = 17)
points(fitted(model)[outliers],  ames$Sale_Price[outliers],  col = "red", pch = 16)

legend("bottomright", legend = c("Leverage", "Influential (Cook's D)", "Outlier"),
       col = c("blue", "orange", "red"), pch = c(1, 17, 16), cex = 0.8)
dev.copy(png, "response_vs_fitted_problematic_original.png", width = 3600, height = 2700, res = 250)
dev.off()
```

## 3) HELPER FUNCTION PLOTS
```{r}
predictors_orig <- c("Year_Built", "Year_Remod_Add", "Gr_Liv_Area", "Garage_Cars", "Lot_Area",
                     "Overall_Qual", "Neighborhood", "Bldg_Type", "Central_Air")

# Gives residuals vs fitted, normal Q-Q, and response vs fitted
diag_plots <- function(model, title = "", file) {
  r <- resid(model)
  f <- fitted(model)
  y <- model.response(model.frame(model))
  par(mfrow = c(1, 3))
  plot(f, r, main = paste("Residuals vs Fitted", title), xlab = "Fitted", ylab = "Residuals")
  abline(h = 0, lty = 2)
  qqnorm(r, main = paste("Normal Q-Q", title)); qqline(r)
  plot(f, y, main = paste("Response vs Fitted", title), xlab = "Fitted", ylab = "Response")
  abline(0, 1, lty = 2); lines(lowess(f, y), col = "red", lwd = 2)
  par(mfrow = c(1, 1))
  dev.copy(png, file, width = 3000, height = 1100, res = 200)
  dev.off()
}

# Gives residuals vs each predictor (predictor list is now an argument)
resid_vs_pred <- function(model, data, predictors, title = "", file) {
  r <- resid(model)
  par(mfrow = c(3, 3))
  for (v in predictors) {
    plot(data[[v]], r, main = paste("Residuals vs", v, title), xlab = v, ylab = "Residuals")
    abline(h = 0, lty = 2)
  }
  par(mfrow = c(1, 1))
  dev.copy(png, file, width = 3000, height = 3000, res = 200)
  dev.off()
}
```

## 4) TRANSFORMATIONS

## 4.1) CHOOSE WHICH TRANSFORMATION FOR RESPONSE (ln vs ^0.2)
```{r}
model_orig <- model   # same model as Section 2
model_log <- lm(Log_Price ~ Year_Built + Year_Remod_Add + Garage_Cars + Lot_Area + Neighborhood +
        Bldg_Type + Central_Air + Overall_Qual * Gr_Liv_Area, data = ames)
model_0.2 <- lm(Price_0.2 ~ Year_Built + Year_Remod_Add + Garage_Cars + Lot_Area + Neighborhood +
        Bldg_Type + Central_Air + Overall_Qual * Gr_Liv_Area, data = ames)

# signif() instead of round(): log/0.2 coefficients are tiny and would round to 0
sum_orig <- summary(model_orig)
coefs <- coef(sum_orig)                      # the coefficient table as a matrix
signif(coefs[!grepl("^Neighborhood", rownames(coefs)), ], 3)

sum_log <- summary(model_log)
coefs <- coef(sum_log)
signif(coefs[!grepl("^Neighborhood", rownames(coefs)), ], 3)

sum_0.2 <- summary(model_0.2)
coefs <- coef(sum_0.2)
signif(coefs[!grepl("^Neighborhood", rownames(coefs)), ], 3)

diag_plots(model_orig, "original", "res_norm_plots_orig.png")
diag_plots(model_log, "(ln)", "res_norm_plots_ln.png")
diag_plots(model_0.2, "(^0.2)",  "res_norm_plots_0.2.png")

resid_vs_pred(model_orig, ames, predictors_orig, "original", "resid_vs_pred_orig.png")
resid_vs_pred(model_log,  ames, predictors_orig, "(ln)",     "resid_vs_pred_ln.png")
resid_vs_pred(model_0.2,  ames, predictors_orig, "(^0.2)",   "resid_vs_pred_0.2.png")

# DECISION: ln(Sale_Price) chosen. Both ln and ^0.2 remove the funnel in residuals vs fitted
# and straighten the Q-Q plot similarly (confirm with plots above), and ln keeps the
# coefficients interpretable as % changes in price. AIC/adj R^2 are NOT used here because
# they cannot compare models with different responses.

# Pairwise scatterplots manually for each numerical predictor
par(mfrow = c(4, 3), mar = c(4, 4, 2, 1))

plot(x = ames$Year_Built, y = ames$Year_Remod_Add,
     main = "Year Remodelled vs Year Built",
     xlab = "Year_Built", ylab = "Year_Remod_Add")

plot(x = ames$Year_Built, y = ames$Gr_Liv_Area,
     main = "Above Ground Living Area vs Year Built",
     xlab = "Year_Built", ylab = "Gr_Liv_Area")

plot(x = ames$Year_Built, y = ames$Garage_Cars,
     main = "Car capacity in Garage vs Year Built",
     xlab = "Year_Built", ylab = "Garage_Cars")

plot(x = ames$Year_Built, y = ames$Lot_Area,
     main = "Lot Area vs Year Built",
     xlab = "Year_Built", ylab = "Lot_Area")

plot(x = ames$Year_Remod_Add, y = ames$Gr_Liv_Area,
     main = "Above Ground Living Area vs Year Remodelled",
     xlab = "Year_Remod_Add", ylab = "Gr_Liv_Area")

plot(x = ames$Year_Remod_Add, y = ames$Garage_Cars,
     main = "Car capacity in Garage vs Year Remodelled",
     xlab = "Year_Remod_Add", ylab = "Garage_Cars")

plot(x = ames$Year_Remod_Add, y = ames$Lot_Area,
     main = "Lot Area vs Year Remodelled",
     xlab = "Year_Remod_Add", ylab = "Lot_Area")

plot(x = ames$Gr_Liv_Area, y = ames$Garage_Cars,
     main = "Car capacity in Garage vs Above Ground Living Area",
     xlab = "Gr_Liv_Area", ylab = "Garage_Cars")

plot(x = ames$Gr_Liv_Area, y = ames$Lot_Area,
     main = "Lot Area vs Above Ground Living Area",
     xlab = "Gr_Liv_Area", ylab = "Lot_Area")

plot(x = ames$Garage_Cars, y = ames$Lot_Area,
     pch = 16, cex = 0.5, col = rgb(0, 0, 0, 0.2),
     main = "Lot Area vs Car capacity in Garage",
     xlab = "Garage_Cars", ylab = "Lot_Area")
dev.copy(png, "conditional_mean_predictor_original.png", width = 3600, height = 2700, res = 250)
dev.off()
par(mfrow = c(1, 1), mar = c(5, 4, 4, 2) + 0.1)   # reset layout and margins
```

## 4.2) CHECK IF ANY NUMERICAL PREDICTORS REQUIRE TRANSFORMATION
```{r}
# How skewed are numerical predictors ?
par(mfrow = c(2, 3))
hist(ames$Year_Remod_Add,   main = "Year_Remod_Add",   xlab = "year")
hist(ames$Year_Built,       main = "Year_Built",       xlab = "year")
hist(ames$Lot_Area,         main = "Lot_Area",         xlab = "sq ft")
hist(ames$Gr_Liv_Area,      main = "Gr_Liv_Area",      xlab = "sq ft")
hist(log(ames$Lot_Area),    main = "log(Lot_Area)",    xlab = "log sq ft")
hist(log(ames$Gr_Liv_Area), main = "log(Gr_Liv_Area)", xlab = "log sq ft")
par(mfrow = c(1, 1))

# Box-Cox on the skewed predictors
par(mfrow = c(1, 2))
boxcox_lot <- boxCox(lm(Lot_Area ~ 1, data = ames), main = "Box-Cox: Lot_Area")
boxcox_liv <- boxCox(lm(Gr_Liv_Area ~ 1, data = ames), main = "Box-Cox: Gr_Liv_Area")
par(mfrow = c(1, 1))

# Best lambda for each
round(boxcox_lot$x[which.max(boxcox_lot$y)], 2)
# log transformation for Lot_Area justified as Box-Cox gives ~ 0.14 (close to 0)
ames$Log_Lot <- log(ames$Lot_Area)

round(boxcox_liv$x[which.max(boxcox_liv$y)], 2)
# Gr_Liv_Area is kept on its raw scale even though Box-Cox suggests a power transformation:
# (1) residuals vs Gr_Liv_Area show no curvature or funnel, and (2) it is our variable of
# interest in the interaction, so the raw scale keeps the slopes interpretable (% per sq ft).
```

## 5) MULTICOLLINEARITY (Module 7)
```{r}
# VIF = 1 / (1 - R^2_j) for each numeric predictor.
numerical_preds <- c("Year_Built", "Year_Remod_Add", "Gr_Liv_Area", "Garage_Cars", "Log_Lot")
all_preds <- c(numerical_preds, "Overall_Qual", "Neighborhood", "Bldg_Type", "Central_Air")

vif_value <- function(pred) {
  others <- setdiff(all_preds, pred)
  r2 <- summary(lm(reformulate(others, response = pred), data = ames))$r.squared
  1 / (1 - r2)
}

vifs <- round(sapply(numerical_preds, vif_value), 2)
vifs   # Year_Built is just above 5 (~5.8); all others < 5

# DECISION: keep both Year_Built and Year_Remod_Add.
# - Year_Built's VIF is only slightly above the cutoff of 5.
# - Both are control variables, not the variables of interest. Multicollinearity inflates
#   THEIR standard errors, but does not affect the Overall_Qual x Gr_Liv_Area estimates.
# - Partial F-tests in Section 6 show each one significantly improves the fit.
```

## 6) MODEL SELECTION (Partial F-tests + Module 9 measures)
```{r}
model_full <- model_log_lot   # ln(price) model with log(Lot_Area)

# No Year_Remod_Add
model_noRem <- update(model_full, . ~ . - Year_Remod_Add)
cat("Partial F-test for Year_Remod_Add\n")
print(anova(model_noRem, model_full)) # very small p-value, so keep it

# No Year_Built
model_noBlt <- update(model_full, . ~ . - Year_Built)
cat("Partial F-test for Year_Built\n")
print(anova(model_noBlt, model_full)) # very small p-value, so keep it

# No Interaction Term
model_noInt <- update(model_full, . ~ . - Overall_Qual:Gr_Liv_Area)

# KEY TEST FOR THE RESEARCH QUESTION: does the living-area slope differ by quality?
cat("Partial F-test for the interaction term\n")
print(anova(model_noInt, model_full)) # small p-value: the interaction significantly improves fit

# Module 9 likelihood-based measures (same extractAIC() function for every model)
crit <- function(m) {
  n <- nobs(m); p <- length(coef(m)) - 1
  aic <- extractAIC(m, k = 2)[2]
  c(Adj_R2 = summary(m)$adj.r.squared,
    AIC    = aic,
    AICc   = aic + 2 * (p + 2) * (p + 3) / (n - p - 1),
    BIC    = extractAIC(m, k = log(n))[2])
}
crit_table <- round(rbind(Full           = crit(model_full),
                          No_Year_Remod  = crit(model_noRem),
                          No_Year_Built  = crit(model_noBlt),
                          No_Interaction = crit(model_noInt)), 3)
knitr::kable(crit_table, caption = "Adjusted R^2, AIC, AICc and BIC for candidate models") %>%
  kable_styling(full_width = FALSE)
# Full model should have the highest Adj R^2 and lowest AIC/AICc/BIC (confirm in output)

# Other predictors are not tested: they were chosen from the literature and the research
# question, not by searching the data. Automated selection (stepAIC) was not used because
# it ignores context and makes later p-values too optimistic (Module 9, slides 45-48),
# so our p-values remain valid.
```

## 7.b) COEFFICIENT TABLE FOR FINAL MODEL (FOR POSTER)
```{r}
coefficients <- summary(model_final)$coefficients
CI <- confint(model_final)

# Find the interaction name safely (R may write it as Overall_Qual...:Gr_Liv_Area)
int_excellent <- grep("^Overall_QualExcellent:Gr_Liv_Area$|^Gr_Liv_Area:Overall_QualExcellent$",
                      rownames(coefficients), value = TRUE)

kept_coefs <- c("Year_Built", "Gr_Liv_Area", "Garage_Cars", "Year_Remod_Add",
                "Log_Lot", "Central_AirY",
                "Overall_QualExcellent", int_excellent, "Bldg_TypeDuplex")

est <- coefficients[kept_coefs, "Estimate"]
table_compact <- data.frame(
  Estimate     = signif(est, 3),
  Pct_change   = round(100 * (exp(est) - 1), 3),   # % change in sale price
  SE           = signif(coefficients[kept_coefs, "Std. Error"], 3),
  Lower_95_CI  = signif(CI[kept_coefs, 1], 3),
  Upper_95_CI  = signif(CI[kept_coefs, 2], 3),
  p_value      = ifelse(coefficients[kept_coefs, "Pr(>|t|)"] < 0.001, "<0.001",
                        round(coefficients[kept_coefs, "Pr(>|t|)"], 3))
) %>%
  rename("% change in price" = Pct_change,
         "Std. Err" = SE,
         "Lower 95% CI" = Lower_95_CI,
         "Upper 95% CI" = Upper_95_CI,
         "p-value" = p_value)

rownames(table_compact) <- c("Year built",
                             "Living area slope (Average quality baseline)",
                             "Garage capacity (cars)",
                             "Year remodelled", "ln(Lot area) (ln(sq ft))", "Air Conditioning=yes",
                             "Quality=excellent (vs Average)",
                             "Living area × Excellent quality",
                             "Building type=duplex (vs single-family)")

knitr::kable(table_compact,
             format = "html",
             caption = "Selected coefficients from the final model (response: ln(Sale_Price)), with % change in price, Standard Errors, 95% Confidence Intervals, and p-values",
             align = "r"
             ) %>%
  kable_styling(full_width = FALSE, position = "center")
```

```{r}
knitr::kable(ames[out_and_lev, c("Sale_Price", "Gr_Liv_Area", "Overall_Qual", "Neighborhood", "Sale_Condition")],
             caption = "Houses that are both outliers and leverage points") %>%
  kable_styling(full_width = FALSE)

# DECISION: flagged houses are KEPT. They are valid recorded sales (no data-entry errors),
# and Cook's distance flags few/no points, so no single house drives the results.
# Removing them only because they don't fit the model would bias the estimates.

par(mfrow = c(1, 1))
plot(fitted(model_final), ames$Log_Price, pch = 16, cex = 0.5, col = "grey70",
     main = "Response vs Fitted, problematic observations highlighted (final model)",
     xlab = "Fitted ln(Sale_Price)", ylab = "ln(Sale_Price)")
abline(0, 1, lty = 2, lwd = 2)

points(fitted(model_final)[leverage],  ames$Log_Price[leverage],  col = "blue", pch = 1)
points(fitted(model_final)[infl_cook], ames$Log_Price[infl_cook], col = "orange", pch = 17)
points(fitted(model_final)[outliers],  ames$Log_Price[outliers],  col = "red", pch = 16)

legend("bottomright", legend = c("Leverage", "Influential (Cook's D)", "Outlier"),
       col = c("blue", "orange", "red"), pch = c(1, 17, 16), cex = 0.8)
dev.copy(png, "response_vs_fitted_problematic_final.png", width = 3600, height = 2700, res = 250)
dev.off()
```

## 9) ANSWER THE RESEARCH QUESTION: living-area slope for each quality level
```{r}
# Copy with quality in natural order (Very_Poor -> Very_Excellent) for plotting only
plot_df <- ames
plot_df$Overall_Qual <- factor(plot_df$Overall_Qual, levels = qual_levels)

# ORIGINAL SCALE
p_orig <- ggplot(plot_df, aes(x = Gr_Liv_Area, y = Sale_Price, colour = Overall_Qual)) +
  geom_point(alpha = 0.15, size = 0.6) +
  geom_smooth(method = "lm", se = FALSE, linewidth = 0.9) +
  scale_colour_viridis_d() +
  labs(x = "Above-ground living area (sq ft)", y = "Sale price", colour = "Overall quality")
print(p_orig)
ggsave("scatter_quality_original.png", p_orig, width = 7.5, height = 6, dpi = 200)

# LOG SCALE (descriptive, other predictors not accounted)
p_log <- ggplot(plot_df, aes(x = Gr_Liv_Area, y = Log_Price, colour = Overall_Qual)) +
  geom_point(alpha = 0.15, size = 0.6) +
  geom_smooth(method = "lm", se = FALSE, linewidth = 0.9) +
  scale_colour_viridis_d() +
  labs(x = "Above-ground living area (sq ft)", y = "ln(Sale price)", colour = "Overall quality")
print(p_log)
ggsave("scatter_quality_log.png", p_log, width = 7.5, height = 6, dpi = 200)

# SLOPE OF LIVING AREA FOR EACH QUALITY LEVEL (same fit as the final model, reparameterized
# so each quality level gets its own living-area slope directly)
model_slopes <- lm(Log_Price ~ Year_Built + Year_Remod_Add + Garage_Cars + Log_Lot +
                     Neighborhood + Bldg_Type + Central_Air +
                     Overall_Qual + Overall_Qual:Gr_Liv_Area, data = ames)

# Pull out the living-area slope for each quality level (natural order), with 95% CIs
slope_names <- paste0("Overall_Qual", qual_levels, ":Gr_Liv_Area")
slopes <- coef(model_slopes)[slope_names]
ci     <- confint(model_slopes)[slope_names, ]

# Convert to % change in price per extra 100 sq ft
slope_table <- data.frame(n_sales         = as.integer(table(ames$Overall_Qual)[qual_levels]),
                          Pct_per_100sqft = round(100 * (exp(100 * slopes) - 1), 2),
                          Lower_95        = round(100 * (exp(100 * ci[, 1]) - 1), 2),
                          Upper_95        = round(100 * (exp(100 * ci[, 2]) - 1), 2))
rownames(slope_table) <- qual_levels

knitr::kable(slope_table,
             caption = "Estimated % change in sale price per extra 100 sq ft, by overall quality (final model)") %>%
  kable_styling(full_width = FALSE)

# NOTE: Very_Poor and Very_Excellent have few sales, so their slopes have wide CIs and
# should be interpreted with caution (limitation).
```
